skill.name: ddd-context-mapping
skill.description: Map bounded context relationships, integration patterns, contract ownership, translation boundaries, failure modes, and versioning policies.
skill.summary: Create practical DDD context maps for service boundaries and integration decisions.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Unclear service boundaries cause domain leakage and fragile integrations. This skill maps relationships, contract ownership, translations, failures, and versioning policies.
actual_capabilities: Lists bounded context pairs and identifies dependency direction.
Selects DDD relationship patterns for each context pair.
Defines contract ownership and translation boundaries.
Plans anti-corruption layers that protect local domain language.
Documents integration failures, fallback behavior, coupling risks, and versioning policies.
limitations: Does not design detailed API schemas or message formats.
Does not replace discussions between teams that own connected contexts.
Does not cover internal class design within one bounded context.
Requires revision when system dependencies or team ownership change.

use_cases.title: Design Service Integrations
use_cases.description: Map upstream and downstream dependencies before teams define service contracts.

use_cases.title: Protect Domain Boundaries
use_cases.description: Identify translation needs and anti-corruption layers around external models.

use_cases.title: Plan System Migration
use_cases.description: Document temporary relationships, ownership, fallbacks, and versioning during incremental modernization.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Context Relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: List the bounded contexts in [system]. For each connected pair, identify the upstream context, downstream context, dependency, and exchanged business capability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a context map from a known system description.

prompt_templates.title: Select Mapping Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Map relationships among [contexts]. Choose a DDD context mapping pattern for each pair and explain ownership, coordination needs, and coupling risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare integration choices across several bounded contexts.

prompt_templates.title: Design Translation Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an anti-corruption layer between [external context] and [local context]. Define translated concepts, boundary ownership, failure handling, and required contract tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prevent an upstream model from leaking into a local domain.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Governed Context Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete context map for [system]. Include every relationship, contract owner, translation rule, failure mode, fallback, versioning policy, and mitigation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an architecture review artifact for a complex system.

output_examples.input: Map how Checkout depends on Billing and Inventory.
output: Billing is upstream of Checkout through a customer-supplier relationship. Billing owns the payment contract.
Inventory is upstream of Checkout through a conformist relationship. Checkout accepts the published availability model.
Checkout translates billing failures into local order states and uses a reservation timeout for inventory failures.

output_examples.input: Protect the Claims context from a legacy Policy system.
output_examples.output: Place an anti-corruption layer at the Claims boundary. Translate legacy policy terms into Claims language, isolate failures, and verify mappings with contract tests.

output_examples.input: Define governance for Catalog events consumed by Search.
output_examples.output: Catalog owns the published event language. Search owns its local projection, supports two event versions, and alerts on rejected or delayed events.

best_practices: Name every upstream and downstream context explicitly.
Assign one clear owner to each integration contract.
Review context maps after ownership, dependencies, or business language change.
anti_patterns: Do not select a relationship pattern without documenting dependency direction.
Do not share domain models across contexts only to reduce mapping work.
Do not omit failure behavior and contract versioning from integration decisions.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide context names, responsibilities, dependency directions, exchanged concepts, contract owners, and known integration constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill create API schemas?
faq.answer: No. It defines context relationships and ownership decisions before detailed API or event schema design.

faq.question: Which DDD patterns can it recommend?
faq.answer: It covers partnership, shared kernel, customer-supplier, conformist, anti-corruption layer, open host service, and published language.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define anti-corruption layers, translation ownership, temporary dependencies, fallback behavior, and migration risks.

faq.question: How often should a context map be reviewed?
faq.answer: Review it whenever team ownership, business language, integration contracts, or dependency directions change.

faq.question: Can it resolve organizational disagreements?
faq.answer: No. It documents decisions and tradeoffs, but responsible teams must agree on ownership and coordination.
